key_insight: For fast surface waves, a thin viscous Stokes layer supplies the phase shift driving momentum from waves to air, with leading-order form stress scaling as the inverse square root of the wave Reynolds number.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers an analytical route to predicting wave-coherent airflow and momentum exchange in simulations where classical critical-layer descriptions may not apply.
method: Apply WKBJ analysis to the viscous Orr–Sommerfeld equation in wave-following coordinates.
Combine an outer Rayleigh mode with a thin Stokes layer and match a near-surface long-wave expansion to the outer solution.
Use a constant-stress effective viscosity in the Stokes layer for wall-modelled simulations.
evidence_signal: Using DNS and wave-phase-resolved LES mean profiles, the framework closely reproduces numerical and available simulated velocity and pressure responses, while predicted form-stress coefficients agree well with available LES estimates.
watch_item: Predictions require a prescribed mean wind profile, and wall-modelled applications depend on the effective-viscosity treatment near the surface.
paper_title: An analytical framework for wave-coherent airflow over fast surface waves
